AND RECOVERY OF WOMEN
AND CHILDREN AS VICTIMS
OF ACTS OF VIOLENCE IN
INDRAMAYU REGENCY.
CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation what is meant by:
1. Region is Indramayu Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Regent together with Regional Apparatus as elements of regional government administration.
3. Regent is the Regent of Indramayu.
4. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is the Regional House of Representatives of Indramayu Regency as an element of Regional Government administration.
5. Agency is the Regional Apparatus Working Unit authorized in the field of Prevention, Protection and Recovery of Women and Children as Victims of Acts of Violence in Indramayu Regency.
6. Woman is an adult human being of female sex and a person recognized by law as a woman.
7. Child is a person who has not reached 18 years of age, including a child in the womb and marriage cannot change the status of a child.
8. Prevention is activities carried out to prevent the occurrence of acts of violence against women and children.
9. Recovery is rehabilitating victims until they are physically and/or psychologically healthy and accepted by society again.
10. Protection is activities and/or actions in order to protect women and children from violence and exploitation.
11. Violence is any act that results in or causes misery and suffering whether physical, sexual, psychological including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or in private life.
12. Physical violence is any act that results in pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage or fainting and/or causes death.
13. Psychological violence is an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, distrust or severe psychological suffering in a person.
14. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual relations, whether unnatural or unwanted with another person for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.
15. Victim is a woman and child who experiences acts of violence, whether physical, psychological or sexual violence.
16. Service is immediate activities and actions carried out by professional personnel in accordance with their respective professions in the form of counseling, therapy and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of victims of violence.
17. Assistance is activities and actions carried out by assistants during the service process.
18. Assistant is a person or representative from an institution who has the expertise to provide assistance.
19. Institution is an agency/body and/or non-governmental organization (NGO) that provides assistance.
20. Integrated Service Center hereinafter abbreviated as PPT, is an institution providing services to victims of violence based in hospitals, managed jointly in the form of medical services (including medico-legal), psychosocial and legal services.
21. Safe house (Shelter) is temporary housing, provided to give protection to victims in accordance with predetermined standards.
22. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations.
23. P2TP2A is one form of service facility for women and children in efforts to fulfill information and needs in the fields of education, health, economy, law, protection and handling of acts of violence and trafficking against women and children.

HEAD OF LEGAL DIVISION OF REGIONAL SECRETARIAT
INDRAMAYU REGENCY
SUNARDI, SH
NIP. 19590411 198503 1 005
ELUCIDATION
ON
REGIONAL REGULATION OF INDRAMAYU REGENCY NUMBER: 18 OF 2012
CONCERNING
PREVENTION, PROTECTION AND RECOVERY OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN
AS VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE IN INDRAMAYU REGENCY
I. GENERAL
The State has an obligation to provide a sense of security to its citizens from threats and actions that can disturb and damage security, psychological, physical, sexual, and economic wellbeing. This is philosophically stated in the preamble of the 1945 Constitution, that the purpose of establishing the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia is to protect the entire nation and the entire homeland of Indonesia.

Because the Indonesian government has signed the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR 1948) and ratified CEDAW (Law Number 7 of 1984 concerning the elimination of all forms of Discrimination against Women), it is obligated to fulfill these provisions. The enforcement and fulfillment of Human Rights is the responsibility of the State.

Through Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection, the government recognizes the existence of children's rights. Human Rights inherent in children include, among others, basic rights as human beings, namely the Right to life, the Right to Growth and Development, the Right to Protection and the Right to Participation.

To fulfill the right to life, children require food in sufficient quantities, healthy and nutritious, as well as optimal health access. Protection from violence that threatens their safety and health must be provided from an early age. Protection is provided to prevent violence and physical, mental and sexual exploitation. To fulfill the right to growth and development, children require space to play, exercise, and education that is appropriate to their physical and psychological development. In fulfilling children's rights, every government administrator, society and parents are obligated to understand and care about children's rights. The existence of legal instruments and law enforcement officials who defend the interests of children is necessary for this protection effort. Legislation that is principled on defending the best interests of the child (The best Interest of Child) is necessary to realize protection that is legal in nature.

Furthermore, it is not uncommon to find cases of women and children who experience problems of physical, psychological, sexual and social violence. For example, women and children victims of persecution, neglect, eviction and abuse by parents or others. For women and children who experience these problems, the government must provide a Safe House (Children protection home) or integrated service center for women and children (P2TP2A) for women and children victims of violence. A Safe House (shelter) is a safe place and is Friendly (friendly) in nature for women and children.

The Integrated Service Center is equipped with companions from educators, doctors, psychologists, religious leaders/clergy and is networked with lawyers for women and children as well as the RPK Unit at the Police.

The fate of women and children victims of violence must be given attention by the government. The large number of cases of violence against women and children are often caused by factors that develop in society, for example low levels of economy, education, environments located in the industrial sector. Therefore victims of violence like this need to receive protection in accordance with the principles of truth, justice, legal certainty, equality and upholding Human Rights.

From the above framework, the regional government is responsible for taking actions both legally, politically, economically and socially to prevent, suppress, reduce, and eliminate all forms of violence against women. One of these efforts is the realization of a legal framework in the implementation of protection for women and children victims of violence.

CHAPTER IV
OBLIGATIONS AND AUTHORITY
OF REGIONAL GOVERNMENT
Article 5
(1) Regional Government is obligated to implement efforts to prevent the occurrence of violence against women and children in the form of:
a. collecting data and information about women and children victims of violence; b. conducting socialization of laws and regulations related to the implementation of prevention, protection and recovery of women and children as victims of violence and exploitation; c. conducting socialization about understanding and values of anti-violence against Women and Children through IEC (information, education and communication) both through community, schools and universities;
d. conducting monitoring and evaluation of the implementation of prevention, protection and recovery of women and children as victims of violence and exploitation.
(2) Regional Government in anticipating the occurrence of acts of violence against Women and Children, has the authority to provide and organize services for victims in the form of:
a. providing and facilitating the establishment of integrated service institutions for victims of acts of violence by involving institutions and community elements;
b. encouraging community awareness of the importance of protection for victims of acts of violence;
c. conducting community empowerment for prevention of acts of violence.
(3) The obligations and authority of Regional Government shall be implemented by the Agency

CHAPTER II
PRINCIPLES AND OBJECTIVES
Article 2
The Implementation of Prevention, Protection and Recovery of Women and Children as Victims of Acts of Violence is carried out based on the principles of:
a. Respect for the rights of the victim;
b. Gender justice and welfare;
c. Non-discrimination; and
d. The best interests of the victim.

Article 7
Forms of prevention of acts of violence against women and children carried out by P2TP2A can be implemented through:
a. socialization activities of laws and regulations and/or regional regulations to the community related to the protection of the rights of women and children;
b. training of P2TP2A members related to the implementation of their duties in preventing acts of violence against women and children.

CHAPTER VII
GUIDANCE, CONTROL AND
SUPERVISION
Article 15
(1) The Regent has the authority to conduct guidance, control and supervision of all activities related to the implementation of prevention, protection and recovery of women and children victims of violence and exploitation in the region.
(2) The authority as referred to in paragraph (1) is technically and operationally implemented by the Agency.

CHAPTER XI
CRIMINAL SANCTIONS
Article 20
(1) Any person who obstructs, disturbs and/or hinders the implementation of programs for the administration of prevention, protection and recovery of women and children victims of acts of violence, shall be threatened with imprisonment for a maximum of 3 (three) months or a fine of at most Rp. 50,000,000.00 (Fifty Million Rupiah).
(2) In addition to criminal acts as referred to in paragraph (1) whether in the form of criminal violations and/or actions that result in losses to the Regional Government, individuals or other parties shall be threatened with criminal law in accordance with the applicable laws and regulations.

Article 8
(1) The Regency P2TP2A, in carrying out its duties and functions, may coordinate with the Religious and Social Welfare Section of the Regional Secretariat of Indramayu Regency, sub-districts, and competent parties in undertaking efforts to prevent acts of violence against women and children.
(2) The mechanism for implementing the prevention duties as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be further regulated by a Regent Regulation.

Article 3
Letter a The “prevention” aspect is a strategic protection effort through:
a. Primary prevention, all people, families, communities and the state in efforts to improve knowledge capacity/ability, understanding, and to ensure that violence against women and children does not occur, including policy socialization, adequate services, supportive workplace policies, and life skills training for women and children.
What is meant by life skills training includes conflict resolution without violence, skills in handling stress, resource management, making effective decisions, effective interpersonal communication, and guidance on the psychosocial development of women and children.
b. Secondary prevention, aimed at community groups with high risk in efforts to improve skills, including training and victim services to ensure that violence against women and children does not occur in the next generation. Activities carried out here include conducting home visits for parents who have just had children to conduct self assessment whether they are at risk of committing violence against children in the future.
c. Tertiary prevention, intended to improve parenting abilities that ensure that violence against women and children does not recur; what is done here is integrated services for women and children who are victims of violence, through counseling, stress-handling management procedures training.
Letter b The “service and assistance” aspect is immediate activities and actions carried out by professional personnel and assistance in accordance with their respective professions in the form of counseling, therapy and advocacy for strengthening and recovery of victims of violence.
Letter c The “recovery” aspect is an effort to restore and recover the physical and mental condition of victims which then reunites them with the victim’s family and community.
Letter d The “empowerment” aspect is a process of increasing the role of the community to participate in the implementation of protection for women and children victims of violence which aims to obtain access and participation in the process of protection of women and children broadly.

CHAPTER VIII
COMMUNITY PARTICIPATION
Article 17
(1) The community may participate in efforts of prevention, protection and recovery of victims of acts of violence against women and children.
(2) Community participation as referred to in paragraph (1) may be carried out by individuals or organizations.
(3) Community participation as referred to in paragraph (2) may be carried out in the form of: a. preventing the occurrence of acts of violence against women and children;
b. submitting reports to the authorities if acts of violence against women and children occur;
c. providing assistance to victims of acts of violence against women and children.

Article 13
(1) In the framework of implementing prevention, protection, and recovery for women and children who are victims of acts of violence in an integrated, harmonious, and continuous manner, the Regional Government establishes Minimum Service Standards (SPM).
(2) Further provisions regarding the Minimum Service Standards as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be further regulated by a Regent Regulation.
(3) The Regional Government is obligated to implement the Minimum Service Standards in Hospitals, Puskesmas (Community Health Centers), NGOs, and Safe Houses (Shelters) designated by the Regent.

Article 6
(1) In the framework of Implementation of prevention, protection and recovery for women and children victims of violence in an integrated, harmonious, and sustainable manner, the Regent establishes P2TP2A at the Regency level.
(2) Further provisions regarding the establishment of P2TP2A management, P2TP2A membership, and P2TP2A working procedures as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be regulated by the Regent.
(3) The Regency P2TP2A may receive case referrals from Hospitals, Community Health Centers, NGOs, Safe Houses (Shelters) and the Community.

Article 19
Sufficiently clear

Article 2
- What is meant by "Respect for the rights of victims" is a series of actions to respect, appreciate and guarantee the fulfillment of the rights of victims.
- What is meant by "Justice and gender equality" is a process to be fair to men and women and equality of conditions for men and women to obtain opportunities and their rights as human beings, so as to be able to play a role and participate in political, economic, social, cultural, defense and National security activities and equality in enjoying the results of such development.
- What is meant by "Non-Discrimination" is an attitude and treatment toward victims by not making distinctions on the basis of age, gender, race, ethnicity, religion and between groups.
- What is meant by "The best interests of victims" is that in all actions concerning victims carried out by regional government, society, legislative bodies and judicial bodies, the best interests of the victim must be the primary consideration.

1.5.rationale: In the original Indonesian text, the definition of “kekerasan” (Pasal 1 angka 11) covers physical, sexual, and psychological suffering (plus threats/coercion/arbitrary deprivation of liberty). It does not define “kekerasan ekonomi”/economic violence as a form of violence. The only economic-related content is (i) the general explanation mentioning threats that can disturb “ekonomi” (economic wellbeing) and (ii) service provision for “kemandirian ekonomi” (Pasal 9 huruf e) and P2TP2A’s scope including “ekonomi” needs (Pasal 1 angka 23). Those are about economic impacts/support, not classifying economic violence/exploitation/neglect as a violence type. Therefore a “Yes” golden label for ‘Economic violence’ appears inconsistent with the policy text; the judge’s ‘No’ is aligned with the document.

3.2.evaluator_rationale: While the text mentions coordination/networking with the police (RPK Unit) in an explanatory section, it does not establish or describe a specialised service unit for VAW victims within police offices.

3.2.rationale: The Indonesian policy does not establish a specialised police unit/service for VAW victims. It mentions in the explanatory section that the integrated service center is “berjaring dengan ... Unit RPK di Kepolisian” (networked with the RPK Unit at the Police), but this is not a normative provision creating/mandating a police-based specialised service unit, nor does it describe such a unit’s functions within police offices. The operative articles focus on P2TP2A services and coordination mainly with health centers (Pasal 10) and other parties (Pasal 8). Thus the judge’s ‘No’ is reasonable; the golden ‘Yes’ likely over-credits a non-operative networking mention.

3.8.evaluator_rationale: The candidate sentences do not describe religious or spiritual counselling/guidance as a service for victims; references to religious leaders appear only in an explanatory networking context and not as a defined counselling service.

Letter d What is meant by "continuous handling up to the rehabilitation stage" is handling that does not stop until physical and psychological recovery, but until the victim can resume life in society including the restoration of their good name.
Letter e What is meant by "confidential handling" is an effort to guarantee certainty for victims that their identity, medical treatment and legal handling will not be disseminated.
Letter f What is meant by "obtaining psychological assistance" is assistance provided by psychologists to victims suffering from trauma/other mental problems to restore the victim's mental condition. While legal assistance is assistance provided by persons and/or legal aid institutions to persons at every level of examination and throughout the legal process.
Letter g What is meant by "guarantee of rights related to victim status" is an effort to provide certainty and protection for victims as members of families and society.

Article 3
Letter a The “prevention” aspect is a strategic protection effort through:
a. Primary prevention, all people, families, communities and the state in efforts to improve knowledge capacity/ability, understanding, and to ensure that violence against women and children does not occur, including policy socialization, adequate services, supportive workplace policies, and life skills training for women and children.

AS VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE IN INDRAMAYU REGENCY
I. GENERAL
The State has an obligation to provide a sense of security to its citizens from threats and actions that can disturb and damage security, psychological, physical, sexual, and economic wellbeing. This is philosophically stated in the preamble of the 1945 Constitution, that the purpose of establishing the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia is to protect the entire nation and the entire homeland of Indonesia.

Because the Indonesian government has signed the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR 1948) and ratified CEDAW (Law Number 7 of 1984 concerning the elimination of all forms of Discrimination against Women), it is obligated to fulfill these provisions. The enforcement and fulfillment of Human Rights is the responsibility of the State.

Through Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection, the government recognizes the existence of children's rights. Human Rights inherent in children include, among others, basic rights as human beings, namely the Right to life, the Right to Growth and Development, the Right to Protection and the Right to Participation.

To fulfill the right to life, children require food in sufficient quantities, healthy and nutritious, as well as optimal health access. Protection from violence that threatens their safety and health must be provided from an early age. Protection is provided to prevent violence and physical, mental and sexual exploitation. To fulfill the right to growth and development, children require space to play, exercise, and education that is appropriate to their physical and psychological development. In fulfilling children's rights, every government administrator, society and parents are obligated to understand and care about children's rights. The existence of legal instruments and law enforcement officials who defend the interests of children is necessary for this protection effort. Legislation that is principled on defending the best interests of the child (The best Interest of Child) is necessary to realize protection that is legal in nature.

Furthermore, it is not uncommon to find cases of women and children who experience problems of physical, psychological, sexual and social violence. For example, women and children victims of persecution, neglect, eviction and abuse by parents or others. For women and children who experience these problems, the government must provide a Safe House (Children protection home) or integrated service center for women and children (P2TP2A) for women and children victims of violence. A Safe House (shelter) is a safe place and is Friendly (friendly) in nature for women and children.

The Integrated Service Center is equipped with companions from educators, doctors, psychologists, religious leaders/clergy and is networked with lawyers for women and children as well as the RPK Unit at the Police.

The fate of women and children victims of violence must be given attention by the government. The large number of cases of violence against women and children are often caused by factors that develop in society, for example low levels of economy, education, environments located in the industrial sector. Therefore victims of violence like this need to receive protection in accordance with the principles of truth, justice, legal certainty, equality and upholding Human Rights.

From the above framework, the regional government is responsible for taking actions both legally, politically, economically and socially to prevent, suppress, reduce, and eliminate all forms of violence against women. One of these efforts is the realization of a legal framework in the implementation of protection for women and children victims of violence.

Article 12
Letter a - What is meant by "quick" is immediate action taken without being convoluted, or with procedures simplified.
- What is meant by "safe" is a guarantee of service protection that feels comfortable, is not disturbed, and is served in a friendly manner, with respect and appreciation.
- What is meant by "empathy" is actions of appreciating, respecting, caring, being friendly, and making happy that aim to please and calm the hearts of victims.
Letter b What is meant by "guarantee of confidentiality" is an effort to guarantee certainty for victims that their identity, medical care and legal handling will not be disseminated.
Letter c What is meant by "easily accessible" is the provision of services and assistance for all people regardless of their social status, so that such services are affordable for the underprivileged or relatively sufficient for the privileged.
Letter d What is meant by "no fees charged" is that service provision and assistance activities carried out by PPT are not charged to victims.

Article 2
- What is meant by "Respect for the rights of victims" is a series of actions to respect, appreciate and guarantee the fulfillment of the rights of victims.
- What is meant by "Justice and gender equality" is a process to be fair to men and women and equality of conditions for men and women to obtain opportunities and their rights as human beings, so as to be able to play a role and participate in political, economic, social, cultural, defense and National security activities and equality in enjoying the results of such development.
- What is meant by "Non-Discrimination" is an attitude and treatment toward victims by not making distinctions on the basis of age, gender, race, ethnicity, religion and between groups.
- What is meant by "The best interests of victims" is that in all actions concerning victims carried out by regional government, society, legislative bodies and judicial bodies, the best interests of the victim must be the primary consideration.

OF REGIONAL GOVERNMENT
Article 5
(1) Regional Government is obligated to implement efforts to prevent the occurrence of violence against women and children in the form of:

d. conducting monitoring and evaluation of the implementation of prevention, protection and recovery of women and children as victims of violence and exploitation.
(2) Regional Government in anticipating the occurrence of acts of violence against Women and Children, has the authority to provide and organize services for victims in the form of:
a. providing and facilitating the establishment of integrated service institutions for victims of acts of violence by involving institutions and community elements;
b. encouraging community awareness of the importance of protection for victims of acts of violence;
c. conducting community empowerment for prevention of acts of violence.
(3) The obligations and authority of Regional Government shall be implemented by the Agency

Article 17
(1) The community may participate in efforts of prevention, protection and recovery of victims of acts of violence against women and children.
(2) Community participation as referred to in paragraph (1) may be carried out by individuals or organizations.
(3) Community participation as referred to in paragraph (2) may be carried out in the form of: a. preventing the occurrence of acts of violence against women and children;
b. submitting reports to the authorities if acts of violence against women and children occur;
c. providing assistance to victims of acts of violence against women and children.

14. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual relations, whether unnatural or unwanted with another person for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.
15. Victim is a woman and child who experiences acts of violence, whether physical, psychological or sexual violence.
16. Service is immediate activities and actions carried out by professional personnel in accordance with their respective professions in the form of counseling, therapy and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of victims of violence.
17. Assistance is activities and actions carried out by assistants during the service process.
18. Assistant is a person or representative from an institution who has the expertise to provide assistance.
19. Institution is an agency/body and/or non-governmental organization (NGO) that provides assistance.
20. Integrated Service Center hereinafter abbreviated as PPT, is an institution providing services to victims of violence based in hospitals, managed jointly in the form of medical services (including medico-legal), psychosocial and legal services.
21. Safe house (Shelter) is temporary housing, provided to give protection to victims in accordance with predetermined standards.
22. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations.
23. P2TP2A is one form of service facility for women and children in efforts to fulfill information and needs in the fields of education, health, economy, law, protection and handling of acts of violence and trafficking against women and children.

CHAPTER VII
GUIDANCE, CONTROL AND
SUPERVISION
Article 15
(1) The Regent has the authority to conduct guidance, control and supervision of all activities related to the implementation of prevention, protection and recovery of women and children victims of violence and exploitation in the region.
(2) The authority as referred to in paragraph (1) is technically and operationally implemented by the Agency.

CHAPTER II
PRINCIPLES AND OBJECTIVES
Article 2
The Implementation of Prevention, Protection and Recovery of Women and Children as Victims of Acts of Violence is carried out based on the principles of:
a. Respect for the rights of the victim;
b. Gender justice and welfare;
c. Non-discrimination; and
d. The best interests of the victim.

CHAPTER XI
CRIMINAL SANCTIONS
Article 20
(1) Any person who obstructs, disturbs and/or hinders the implementation of programs for the administration of prevention, protection and recovery of women and children victims of acts of violence, shall be threatened with imprisonment for a maximum of 3 (three) months or a fine of at most Rp. 50,000,000.00 (Fifty Million Rupiah).
(2) In addition to criminal acts as referred to in paragraph (1) whether in the form of criminal violations and/or actions that result in losses to the Regional Government, individuals or other parties shall be threatened with criminal law in accordance with the applicable laws and regulations.

Article 2
- What is meant by "Respect for the rights of victims" is a series of actions to respect, appreciate and guarantee the fulfillment of the rights of victims.
- What is meant by "Justice and gender equality" is a process to be fair to men and women and equality of conditions for men and women to obtain opportunities and their rights as human beings, so as to be able to play a role and participate in political, economic, social, cultural, defense and National security activities and equality in enjoying the results of such development.
- What is meant by "Non-Discrimination" is an attitude and treatment toward victims by not making distinctions on the basis of age, gender, race, ethnicity, religion and between groups.
- What is meant by "The best interests of victims" is that in all actions concerning victims carried out by regional government, society, legislative bodies and judicial bodies, the best interests of the victim must be the primary consideration.

Article 4
Letter a What is meant by "obtaining protection" is obtaining protection from individuals, groups and institutions, both government and non-government.
Letter b What is meant by "obtaining information" is access and explanations/information about the existence of complaint centers, PPT, and all matters related to the fulfillment of their rights and involvement in the decision-making process related to assistance and case developments.
Letter c What is meant by "minimum services" is services that include medical, medicolegal, psychosocial and legal.
Letter d What is meant by "continuous handling up to the rehabilitation stage" is handling that does not stop until physical and psychological recovery, but until the victim can resume life in society including the restoration of their good name.
Letter e What is meant by "confidential handling" is an effort to guarantee certainty for victims that their identity, medical treatment and legal handling will not be disseminated.
Letter f What is meant by "obtaining psychological assistance" is assistance provided by psychologists to victims suffering from trauma/other mental problems to restore the victim's mental condition. While legal assistance is assistance provided by persons and/or legal aid institutions to persons at every level of examination and throughout the legal process.
Letter g What is meant by "guarantee of rights related to victim status" is an effort to provide certainty and protection for victims as members of families and society.

CHAPTER IV

Article 5
(1) Regional Government is obligated to implement efforts to prevent the occurrence of violence against women and children in the form of:
a. collecting data and information about women and children victims of violence; b. conducting socialization of laws and regulations related to the implementation of prevention, protection and recovery of women and children as victims of violence and exploitation; c. conducting socialization about understanding and values of anti-violence against Women and Children through IEC (information, education and communication) both through community, schools and universities;
